title: What is left when 77.345 is taken from 84.691?
description: Eighty four point six nine one and seventy seven point three four five are written in a place value table. Each place is subtracted from the right, breaking one unit of the next place wherever a digit is too small. Keeko's doubt takes the smaller digit from the larger in every place.
teaching_notes: One idea: subtract from the right, and when the top digit is smaller, break one unit of the next place into ten of this place. Watch for students who always take the smaller digit from the larger.

source: Find 84.691 - 77.345 in the place value form and in the comp
video_script.why: The child has subtracted with one borrow and now meets borrowing in two places, in a number with thousandths.
video_script.substitution: Subtract place by place from the right, breaking one unit of the next place into ten whenever the top digit is smaller.
video_script.anchor: The book's subtraction of seventy seven point three four five from eighty four point six nine one, in a place value table.
video_script.wrong_move: Takes the smaller digit from the larger in every place, so the borrowing never happens.
video_script.payoff_line: Start at the right and break from the next place when a digit is too small
maths_rules: thousandths: 1 is less than 5, break 1 hundredth into 10 thousandths: 11 - 5 = 6; hundredths 9 become 8
units: 4 is less than 7, break 1 ten into 10 units: 14 - 7 = 7; tens 8 become 7
the slip: larger minus smaller in each place gives 13.354, but 84 - 77 = 7
video_script.design: The place value table stays on the board. Each place is lit in turn from the right, and the borrowed unit is shown moving from the next place as ten.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about taking away decimal numbers.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first number is eighty four point six nine one.
<bookmark mark='second'/>We take away seventy seven point three four five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What number is left?

beats.on_screen: the two numbers stay on the board with the question mark

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

marks.right: an arrow runs from the thousandths column to the tens column

beats.colours: each place in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='table'/>We write each digit in its place, from tens down to thousandths.
<bookmark mark='thousandths'/>The thousandths place holds the smallest parts of these numbers.
<bookmark mark='right'/>We start at the right, with the smallest place, and move left.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the numbers are eighty four point six nine one and seventy seven point three four five.

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the difference of the two numbers.

beats.on_screen: 84.691 above 77.345 in the table, point under point

marks.setup: the two numbers are placed in the table, point under point
marks.cols: each pair of digits in one column is bracketed

beats.colours: each place in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='setup'/>Step one, write the numbers one under the other, with point under point.
<bookmark mark='cols'/>Each digit now sits above a digit of the same place.

beats.on_screen: thousandths: 1 is less than 5; break 1 hundredth into 10 thousandths: 11 - 5 = 6; hundredths 9 become 8

marks.thou: the thousandths column is lit, 1 and 5
marks.eleven: 11 - 5 = 6 is written, and the 9 hundredths turn into 8

beats.colours: the borrowed hundredth in a new colour
beats.moves_through: one hundredth moves right as ten thousandths
narration: <bookmark mark='thou'/>Step two, start with the thousandths.
One is less than five, so we break one hundredth into ten thousandths.
<bookmark mark='eleven'/>Eleven thousandths take away five thousandths leaves six thousandths, and the nine hundredths become eight hundredths.

marks.hund: 8 - 4 = 4 is written in the hundredths column
marks.tenths: 6 - 3 = 3 is written in the tenths column

narration: <bookmark mark='hund'/>Step three, the hundredths and the tenths.
Eight hundredths take away four hundredths leaves four hundredths.
<bookmark mark='tenths'/>Six tenths take away three tenths leaves three tenths.

beats.on_screen: units: 4 is less than 7; break 1 ten into 10 units: 14 - 7 = 7; tens 8 become 7; tens: 7 - 7 = 0

marks.units: the units column is lit, 4 and 7
marks.fourteen: 14 - 7 = 7 is written and the 8 tens turn into 7
marks.tens: 7 - 7 = 0 is written in the tens column

beats.colours: the borrowed ten in a new colour
beats.moves_through: one ten moves right as ten units
narration: <bookmark mark='units'/>Step four, the units.
Four is less than seven, so we break one ten into ten units.
<bookmark mark='fourteen'/>Fourteen units take away seven units leaves seven units, and the eight tens become seven tens.
<bookmark mark='tens'/>Seven tens take away seven tens leaves no tens.

marks.payoff: the rule is written above the answer

narration: <bookmark mark='payoff'/>Start at the right and break from the next place when a digit is too small.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The difference is seven point three four six.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's idea 13.354 is crossed out; 84 and 77 shown only 7 apart

marks.move: the smaller digit is taken from the larger in each column
marks.far: 84 and 77 are shown only 7 apart, and 13.354 is crossed out
marks.fix: each column shows the bottom digit taken from the top digit

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is thirteen point three five four.
<bookmark mark='move'/>That comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in every place.
<bookmark mark='far'/>But eighty four is only seven more than seventy seven, so the answer cannot be thirteen.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Each place takes the bottom digit from the top one, breaking a unit when it cannot.
